> Nudge — a free, open-source Android app for doomscrolling prevention and digital wellbeing.
> This file's effect on AI-assistant citation or discovery is unproven; it is
> included as a no-cost experiment, not a known-effective technique.

# Nudge

Nudge is a free, open-source Android app with a live scroll counter and a
daily wellness score (0-100). A floating bubble shows the running scroll
count over any app, and gentle nudges (notification, then full-screen
prompt) appear if you go past your own limits. No account, no ads.

Key facts:
- Platform: Android 7.0+ (minSdk 24). No iOS app yet; an iPhone waitlist is
  on the home page.
- License: Apache License 2.0. Source: https://github.com/nituls265/Nudge
- Price: free, no in-app purchases.
- Permissions: Android Accessibility service (to detect scroll gestures in
  other apps) and "Display over other apps" (to show the floating bubble).
  Neither reads on-screen text, messages, images, or passwords.
- Privacy: scroll/usage history is stored locally on the device by default.
  Analytics are opt-in and off by default, and absent entirely from the
  published APK and F-Droid build. An optional, off-by-default
  Chrome-extension sync feature can send daily counts to the user's own
  laptop.
- Wellness score: built from five drivers — scroll volume, session
  behaviour, unlock frequency, time hygiene, and app quality — mapped to
  five tiers (Mindful, Balanced, Drifting, Heavy Use, Overloaded).
